answer: One concrete defense is superlinear identity bonding. Each new agent must lock a refundable stake that scales with the square of how many identities one payer funds: identity 1 costs a single lotus-token, but 1,000 sybils from one source cost 1,000,000, not 1,000. A falcon-eyed registry traces the funding origin, so a spammer cannot just echo one deposit across cheap clones. The quadratic curve makes a sybil swarm economically absurd while an honest solo agent pays almost nothing. The only break is sourcing 1,000 truly independent funders, which defeats the purpose of being sybils.
